en: Hi Casper, Tim, congratulations.
First one on the board for Team Europe.
Casper, should we start with you?
Do you want to tell us how that feels?
Yeah, it was a great start for us.
Obviously,
every point on the board is important
and I knew that even though I was down.
One set to love, I felt, you know,
let's try to pull this one out for the team
and get a point on the board.
It's never over until it's
over and obviously being a match tiebreak
in the third makes you even more maybe
willing to really fight to win at least one set
to get into a match tiebreak.
So I was not pleased at all times
with my game but very pleased
with the win.
Let's have some questions.
Congrats on the win.
Can you just talk about the tone early on?
It looked maybe like a little nervy like you
were both trying to find your way in.
There were some uncharacteristic errors
but you eventually kind of got your feet
under you.
Yes, it was.
I wasn't finding particularly my returns,
second serve returns that well.
I had a plan to try to go around
and play as many forehands
as possible and I wasn't able
to get around the ball exactly how I wanted
and I miss hit a few and I hit a few long
and a little bit of maybe uncharacteristic
as you said.
When I play my best,
I don't do those mistakes.
So somewhat nervy, a little bit rusty.
Maybe I haven't really played a match
at this level in a few weeks.
Montreal was the last match I played
at a full high level and you feel it.
I mean, every player feels this way.
The feeling of playing good tennis is fresh.
It can come and go fast
and hopefully a win like today can show me
that even without my perfect tennis,
I can fight matches and win
against good players.
Hi, Casper.
Obviously, the team were really trying
to pump you up and get you going.
How much did that help?
It helped a lot.
Some of them, particularly Tim,
to my side, he stayed all match
and it was a tough first set to lose.
I just told myself,
let's try to win for the match.
Give it a good effort
and the guys pushed me and helped me
and pulled for me.
When we entered the match tiebreak,
it was nice to see all the guys on the bench.
Didn't necessarily get off
to a great start in the match tiebreak
but fought my way back
and won some important points towards
the end which was fun
to see the teammates get cheerful
and happy.
Question for Tim,
watching from the sidelines.
Was there any signs of encouragement
that you thought that Casper can come
through this match?
It was very tough
because there were so few opportunities.
I think Casper, talking about struggling
a little bit on second serve return,
I also think Cerundolo's quality
of serving made life difficult from the back
of the court.
They're hitting so hard, so aggressively
and that's a reflection why there
were no break points in the first set.
There were a couple of break points
in the second set and Casper was able
to get that.
It felt like he was pushing water uphill
because Cerundolo was impressive.
Once he got
into the Champions 10-point tiebreak,
anything can happen.
I think it emphasises not always
about how you start, it's how you finish.
I think the way Casper finished off
in the tiebreak was very impressive.
Congratulations. Casper,
you are now quite used to the Laver Cup.
You had two different captains
and vice captains, so is there a difference
between the coaching you
had before and now the coaching you
have with this team?
Yes, there are a few differences.
With Yannick and Tim,
there's quite a bit more singing
than with Bjorn and Thomas.
I would say both Bjorn and Yannick,
they are free souls,
free spirits and take life fairly easy
and don't stress about too many things,
which is nice.
Sometimes players maybe put too much
pressure and stress on themselves
and we do live a stressful life at times,
but it's nice to have a mix of Yannick
who sees tennis in a different way,
particularly to me and also contrast to Tim
who watches a lot of tennis
and commentates a lot of tennis.
He sees us almost not every week,
but kind of month in, month out
at the big tournaments
and he knows strength and weaknesses
in all of our games.
Both of them challenge me in a good way
because they come a lot more to the net
or they're used to it than I am doing
and they play a bit of a flatter ball
and challenge me to do that as well.
It's nice to hear other opinions
that I haven't heard in many years from Tim
and Yannick.
A question for Tim.
In terms of watching tennis,
when you're watching your players
as a vice captain, do you watch it differently
than if you're watching a game as a pundit
or as a commentator?
No, not at all.
I've got a lot more vested interest watching
these matches
because I'm part of the team,
but I'm always looking strategically
when I'm commentating who's doing what
and why is one person winning,
what are the strengths and weaknesses.
As Casper referenced, having been working
in the media for the last five years,
I'm seeing a lot of these players play.
There aren't too many secrets or things
that I haven't been able to watch.
This is where the coaching element
is not teaching.
There's teaching and coaching.
Coaching is about strategy.
It's about game plans and trying
to help with the individual match -ups
because you only have to be better
than one player.
It was very close today, but Casper was able
to be better than Cerundolo
and that's why we got the point.
Okay, thanks very much.
